title: Framer's agent now runs on its own, and Figma's reaches Dev Mode
dek: Framer and Figma agents, iOS 27.3's Calendar, Nielsen's ladder, Microsoft's Autopilot, Automattic's AI writing habits, three events.
preheader: Framer's agent works on a schedule, Figma's reaches Dev Mode, and Microsoft draws its AI as a line.
hero_alt: Triangle mountains, a circle sun and pill-shaped swell, a teammate’s cursor selecting them
summary: Framer's agent can now [run on a schedule and act in Slack and Notion](https://www.framer.com/updates/automations-connectors-slack), and Figma's agent [works in Dev Mode](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/37998629035799-Work-with-the-Figma-agent-in-design-files). iOS 27.3 [moves Calendar's main buttons within thumb reach](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/25/ios-27-3-introduces-design-changes-for-these-apple-apps/). And Microsoft explains why [its Autopilot agent is drawn as a line, not a mascot](https://microsoft.design/articles/the-art-of-playing-a-supporting-role/).

learn.intro: Automattic's design writers turned research on AI writing tells into two installable agent skills.
steps: Make the agent ask about audience and voice before writing.

learn.title: Hand a design task to AI, or keep a person on it?
learn.intro: Use Nielsen's verification ladder, then ask whether the feature should think with people or for them.

columns.label: Hand it to AI when
items: A checklist can judge the result in minutes
You want many options and will test to choose

columns.label: Keep a person on it when
items: Only users or the market can judge it
Doing it builds your judgement, as with synthesis
It decides what's worth doing or aligns the team

examples.text: 95% agreement with human auditors, because it is built on human-mapped data.

learn.rule: If you can't say how the output gets judged, keep a person on it.
